Brisbane and the bay

Event Planners in Brisbane

Brisbane runs on a subtropical calendar, which means the comfortable half of the year is also the busy half. Tell us the month before anything else, because here it decides the shortlist, the start time and the contingency all at once, and we will pass the brief to planners who cover your area.

No obligationSending a brief costs nothing and commits you to nothing.
Get event planning quotesHow planning works
  • May to SeptemberThe cool dry window, and the Saturdays inside it go first.
  • November to MarchStorm season, so the wet plan is written in month one.
  • Coast in both directionsThe Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast sit inside supplier travel range.

Choose the month first and the rest of the plan follows.

In most cities a planner asks about the venue. In Brisbane the more useful opening question is which month, because the answer changes the shortlist, the ceremony hour and the contingency together.

The seasons here run the opposite way to the southern capitals, and it shows up in every quote. May to September is cool, dry and predictable, which is why event planners in Brisbane fill those Saturdays first. November to March brings heat, humidity and fast afternoon storms, so a summer brief starts later in the day, keeps guests near shade and water, and names a covered space a hundred people can reach in minutes.

Geography adds the second layer. The river cuts the city into pieces, the cliffs at Kangaroo Point and the ferry network shape how guests actually arrive, and the bay islands turn a straightforward event into a freight job on a timetable. Out past the suburbs, hinterland properties sit at the end of narrow driveways a loaded truck has to turn around in. Send the brief once.

In and around Brisbane

What are you planning in Brisbane?

Six briefs planners here see most often. The month sits behind all of them, and each card links to the national page that sets out how the service works.

Start with

Weddings

A property that is straightforward in August is a different proposition in February. Planners here start with the month, then test the shortlist for air conditioning, genuinely covered space and an indoor option you would actually be happy with. The Saturdays between May and September commit earliest.

Find planners

Parties and milestones

An outdoor birthday through summer is a shade and water problem before it is a styling one, which is why so many start in the morning or after five. Backyard work across Bulimba, West End and Paddington turns on the truck, the power and the noise conditions attached to the address.

Find planners

Corporate events

Conferences, launches, awards nights and staff functions, with a growing share of government and public sector work that comes with its own documentation. Packaged rooms through the CBD and South Bank keep the supplier count low and arrive as a minimum spend rather than a build.

Find planners

Engagement parties

Short notice and a moving guest list, usually a room in Fortitude Valley, Newstead or Teneriffe rather than a build from scratch. Between November and March the useful question is where guests go if a storm arrives, since these are the events most often held half outdoors.

Find planners

Proposals

The good hours are early and late for most of the year. A planner handles the timing, the permissions where the spot is public parkland or a lookout, and the logistics of getting other people into position, which around the cliffs and the river usually means a ferry timetable.

Find planners

Private celebrations

Christenings, anniversaries, wakes, a fiftieth at a club, a family weekend built around interstate flights. Clubs and community halls take a great deal of this work across Redland Bay, Moreton Bay and Ipswich, usually with in house catering rules worth reading before you book anyone.

Planning support

How much help do you want in Brisbane?

Whichever level you buy, the summer contingency has to sit inside it. Between November and March the coordinator owns the weather call, and the useful measure is not whether it rains but how fast a hundred people can move under cover.

Full planning

A planner carries the whole build with you, from the first budget conversation to the last supplier leaving.

Usually engaged nine to fourteen months out.

  • Budget built and tracked
  • Venue and supplier shortlists
  • Contracts and payment schedule
  • Run sheet and floor plan
  • On the day, start to finish

Partial planning

You have made a start. A planner picks up the parts that have stalled and brings the rest into one plan.

Often engaged four to eight months out.

  • Picks up from where you are
  • Fills the supplier gaps
  • Tidies the budget
  • Builds the run sheet
  • Hands back a plan you can follow

On-the-day coordination

Your plan is built. A coordinator takes it over in the final weeks and runs the day so you can be in it.

Usually engaged four to eight weeks out.

  • Reads and stress-tests your plan
  • Confirms every supplier
  • Owns the run sheet
  • First point of contact on the day
  • Handles what goes sideways

Venue sourcing

Planners who know a market can shortlist against your date, your numbers and your budget rather than sending you back to the same search results.

Event coordination

Coordination is the execution layer: suppliers confirmed, a run sheet everyone has, and one person answering questions on the day.

Wedding coordination

A wedding coordinator takes a plan you have already built and runs the day itself, so nobody in the wedding party is directing traffic.

Choosing well

Finding the right planner in Brisbane

Four checks worth running before you shortlist. Two of them are about the month, one is about the driveway, and the fourth is the one people leave until it is too late to fix.

No. 01

Test the shortlist against your worst month

If your date sits between November and March, walk each site as though it is thirty three degrees and a storm is twenty minutes away. Ask what is genuinely covered rather than shaded, whether the indoor option is one you would be happy with, and how long it takes to move a set table and a hundred guests into it.

No. 02

Ask about the access track, not the address

Hinterland and acreage properties often sit at the end of a narrow driveway that a loaded truck has to turn around in, and heavy rain changes what that track will take. Ask what vehicle size the property accepts, whether there is a turning circle, and what happens to access after a wet week.

No. 03

Name who calls the weather, and when

The handover should settle three things in writing: which covered space guests move to, how many minutes the move takes, and the hour a decision is made. Then give one person the authority to make it. Settle what happens to outdoor power at the same time, because that is the part that catches people mid afternoon.

No. 04

Check the pack down window, not just bump in

On public land and in a lot of riverside spaces the pack down window is tighter than the set up window, and nobody reads it until the night. Get both in writing, including the hour the site must be clear, and check whether a truck can return the following morning or everything leaves that night.

Assume speed rather than duration. A Brisbane storm is measured in minutes, and so is your contingency.

On the ground

How the Brisbane calendar reverses

Everything below follows from one fact: the good months here are the cool ones. That inverts the southern pattern, and it changes availability, start times and what a contingency actually has to do.

The season runs backwards

May to September is the outdoor window, and its Saturdays commit long before summer dates do. That is the reverse of Melbourne or Sydney, where the pressure sits in spring and early autumn. From November to March the heat, the humidity and a daily chance of a fast afternoon storm push events later in the day or into a packaged room with air conditioning. Winter here is peak season, so a June wedding is not a bargain, and a July conference is competing with everything else in the cool half of the year.

A city arranged around a river

The river decides how guests move. Kangaroo Point sits under a cliff face, Teneriffe and Bulimba face each other across the water with a ferry between them, and a five kilometre distance on a map can be a long drive in practice. Ferry timetables matter for guest arrival and for the last service of the night. Further out, the bay islands turn an event into freight: everything crosses by ferry or barge, deliveries have cut-off times, and suppliers often arrive a day early, which shows up in their quotes.

What a summer bump in costs you

Heat and humidity slow a crew, and the schedule has to carry it. A job that takes four hours in June takes longer on a thirty three degree afternoon, and a team that has been in the sun since morning is slower by five. Between November and March a fast storm during set up can stop work and soak gear.

  • A wider bump in window than the same job in winter
  • A staging area under cover for equipment
  • Shade and water written into the crew plan
  • A decision made in advance about outdoor power

Questions

Planning an event in Brisbane

How much does an event planner cost in Brisbane?

Lower than the southern capitals on the only guide that publishes city figures. Airtasker's Australian cost guide, updated February 2025, gives Brisbane a median of $1,600 to $1,800, which sits closest to day-of coordination rather than a full build, so treat it as the bottom of the range. Locally, the month moves the figure as much as the guest count does, because a summer event carries a contingency a winter one does not.

What is the best time of year for an outdoor event in Brisbane?

May to September, and that window is why those Saturdays commit first. The cool dry months give you comfortable afternoons, a low storm risk and a crew that works at normal speed. November to March is not off limits, but it is a different plan: a later start, guests kept near shade and water, and a covered space a hundred people can reach in minutes. Book the cool months earlier than you think you need to.

How do we plan around a storm on the day?

Assume speed rather than duration. Name the covered space, time how long it takes to move guests and a set table into it, then set the decision hour from that number and give one person the authority to call it. Settle what happens to outdoor power in the same conversation. A Brisbane storm often passes in under an hour, so the plan is about the twenty minutes before it arrives.

Why does a summer set up in Brisbane take longer?

Because heat and humidity slow the crew down. A bump in that takes four hours in June takes longer on a thirty three degree afternoon, and a team that has been loading since morning is measurably slower by late afternoon. Planners widen the set up window, put shade and water into the crew plan, and ask for a staging area under cover so gear is not sitting in the open when a storm crosses.

Do Brisbane planners work on the Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast?

Most do, and the traffic runs both ways. Both coasts sit inside a normal supplier travel range, roughly an hour or so from the city depending on the address, so a Brisbane planner will quote a hinterland or beachfront job without hesitating and coast based planners take city work in return. Ask what travel adds and whether an overnight stay applies, since a late pack down an hour away often means one.

Can a planner run an event at a riverside venue in Brisbane?

Yes, and access is the first conversation. Riverside and cliff top sites often sit on public land with set hours, noise conditions and a pack down window tighter than the bump in, and a fair number are easier to reach by ferry than by road. Ask where a truck can stop, how far gear has to be carried from that point, and what the last ferry service means for your finish time.
